drop.title: The Cascade That Needs a Crowd

title: The Cascade
That Needs a Crowd
slides.dek: A cold needs one carrier, so on a network it is unstoppable: a single case walks the whole web. But you join the riot, adopt the risky tool, or pull your savings only once several neighbours already have. That one change, needing a few instead of one, flips the physics. Below a sharp seed density the cascade dies in local patches; a hair above, it floods a whole slice of the network at once.

slides.body: A cold is *simple* contagion: one infected neighbour is enough, so on a network one case walks the entire connected web it started in. A single spark takes the whole component. But most things that move through a crowd are not colds. You do not join a protest, buy the costly new phone, or pull your money from a wobbling bank because *one* acquaintance did. You wait until *several* have. Centola and Macy named that complex contagion in 2007; Granovetter wrote the mechanism in 1978, a threshold model where each person needs to see some number of neighbours act before acting too.

Give every node a threshold of two and raise the seed density slowly. For a while almost nothing happens, most dormant nodes never collect two active neighbours at once. Then, between a *7%* seed and an *8%* seed, the board flips: seven percent fizzles, eight percent floods 93% of the graph in a few rounds. Averaged over thousands of graphs the jump becomes a *vertical cliff*, near zero on one side and near the whole graph on the other, a first-order transition. It is the exact activation mirror of the k-core's collapse: one rule peels a network down, this one floods it up, and both leap at their threshold.

lines.sub: direct sequel to #048: run the r-neighbour rule on a random GRAPH, not a lattice, and the transition becomes a discontinuous first-order jump in the seed density. rotates format back to research, ninth in the network-science vein. reuses #045's rng verbatim, deterministic, SSR-safe

three modules over one cascade engine: a live 140-node board where the seed dial only ever adds sparks, a sweep of final active fraction vs seed density at c=5 for n=250/2,000/12,000 with mean-field theory overlaid, and the self-consistency fold where two fixed points collide

checked offline first. z = p + (1-p)·P(Po(cz) >= r) tracks a direct cascade to ~0.003 at n=12,000 above the jump. at c=5 the fold sits at p_c ~ 0.024 for r=2 and ~0.137 for r=3; r=1 floods from the first seed. a genuine saddle-node, three crossings below p_c, two annihilating at it

slides.sub: Module 01 is the cascade live on one 140-node graph, where the seed dial only ever adds sparks. Module 02 sweeps thousands of graphs into the vertical cliff. Module 03 is the payoff: the flood is not the cascade growing faster, it is the low, safe, fizzled state disappearing out from under it, so the system has nowhere to sit but the top. Every graph, cascade and fixed point recomputes in your browser on load.
